neet_che_u06_t03_1.working: By the law of mass action, Kc is products over reactants, each raised to its stoichiometric coefficient: [NH3]^2/([N2][H2]^3).

neet_che_u06_t03_2.working: Reversing the reaction gives 1/16. Halving the equation takes the square root: (1/16)^(1/2) = 0.25.

neet_che_u06_t03_3.working: Qc = (0.2)(0.2)/0.5 = 0.08. Since Qc > Kc = 0.04, the net reaction proceeds backward.

neet_che_u06_t03_4.working: Reversing gives 1/K, multiplying by 2 gives K^2, dividing by 2 gives K^(1/2), and adding reactions gives K x K2. So A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV.

neet_che_u06_t03_5.working: A is false because a catalyst does not change K. B is true because pure solids are omitted. C is true because a small K means reactants predominate. D is false because K depends only on temperature. E is true because Q < K drives the forward reaction.
